kept.excerpt: Compiled for the North Shore/Merrimack Valley news consortium. Massachusetts’ 6th Congressional District primary is September 1, 2026; the general election is November 3, 2026. Rep. Seth Moulton is not seeking re-election to the seat he’s held since 2015; he’s running in the Democratic primary for U.S. Senate against Sen. Ed Markey.
kept.relevance: This near-cutoff voter guide establishes the open-seat context and identifies a primary-date discrepancy with the question’s September 15 date.

kept.excerpt: Today, Dan Koh’s campaign launched a new ad, “Democrats You Trust,” featuring President Biden, Vice President Harris, the Massachusetts AFL-CIO, and local Democratic leaders who have endorsed his campaign for Congress. The new advertising follows a newly released poll that shows Dan with a 19 point lead in the field, building on months of on-the-ground organizing, more than 100 endorsements from labor organizations, elected officials, and community leaders, and a record fundraising operation that has out-paced every other candidate in the race.
kept.publisher: Dan Koh for Congress — campaign press release
kept.relevance: This official candidate source documents Koh’s advertised endorsements and campaign activity close to the cutoff, while its strength claims should be treated as campaign advocacy.

kept.excerpt: According to the campaign, the survey of 400 likely Democratic primary voters was conducted by Global Strategy Group between July 30 and Aug. 2 and has a margin of error of plus or minus 4.9 percentage points. The poll found Koh with 34% support, followed by Beccia at 15% and Nguyen at 14%. Twenty-four percent of respondents were undecided. Campaign-commissioned polls are common during election campaigns and should not be considered independent surveys.
kept.relevance: The latest dated poll located before the cutoff shows Koh ahead but also substantial undecided support and explicit campaign-sponsorship limitations.

kept.excerpt: According to Federal Election Commission filings covering activity through June 30, Koh reported about $3 million cash on hand, the largest campaign treasury in the race. Beccia followed with roughly $2.3 million, much of it from personal loans to his campaign. State Rep. Tram Nguyen, who represents Andover, North Andover, Boxford and part of Tewksbury, reported several hundred thousand dollars available, while Jamie Belsito, Mariah Lancaster and Bethany Andres-Beck each reported substantially smaller cash reserves.
kept.relevance: The reported FEC figures establish Koh’s resource advantage while identifying Beccia’s self-funding as a significant competing source of spending power.

kept.excerpt: Beth Andres-Beck, John Beccia, Dan Koh, Mariah Lancaster, Tram Nguyen, and Jamie Zahlaway Belsito are running in the Democratic primary for Massachusetts' 6th Congressional District on Sept. 1. Incumbent Seth Moulton (D) is running for the U.S. Senate to represent Massachusetts. The election is set against the backdrop of affordability and opposing President Donald Trump's (R) administration.
kept.relevance: This dated election preview establishes the six-way nomination contest and the major issues candidates were using to distinguish themselves.

kept.excerpt: Koh’s campaign said it raised more than $1 million between April and June, bringing its fundraising total to more than $4.5 million since launching the campaign. Nguyen, an Andover Democrat who represents the 18th Essex District in the Massachusetts House, announced Thursday that she raised $266,000 during the second quarter — the largest quarterly total of her campaign. According to her campaign, Nguyen has now raised more than $690,000 since entering the race from 2,827 individual donors.
kept.relevance: These contemporaneous campaign fundraising announcements indicate the scale of Koh’s fundraising lead over Nguyen before the final campaign stretch.

kept.excerpt: The poll, commissioned by Nguyen’s campaign and conducted May 26-27 by Workbench Strategy, found Nguyen leading the six-candidate field with 28% support among likely Democratic primary voters. Former Biden administration official Dan Koh was second at 18%, while 24% of respondents remained undecided. The Workbench poll surveyed 400 likely Democratic primary voters and has a margin of error of plus or minus 4.89 percentage points. Interviews were conducted through a combination of live telephone calls and text invitations to an online survey.
kept.relevance: This earlier rival-sponsored poll provides counterevidence to Koh’s August internal poll and shows why the polls cannot be treated as a consistent independent trend.

kept.excerpt: Massachusetts is holding U.S. House primaries on Sept. 1, 2026. In Massachusetts, the winner of a primary election is the candidate who receives the greatest number of votes, even if the candidate does not receive an outright majority of votes cast.
kept.relevance: Plurality nomination rules mean Koh could win the crowded Democratic contest without reaching majority support.

search_notes: Frozen cutoff: 2026-08-19. Included only individually dated articles and releases published on or before that date; excluded later reporting, outcome material, prediction-market pages, undated aggregators, and live financial summaries without a qualifying publication date. Publication dates and excerpts were verified in web_search indexed source text. web_fetch failed because its provider was not configured; the requested agent-reach web read fallback returned RATE_LIMITED, so full-page retrieval was unavailable. Campaign statements and both polls are explicitly attributed to their sponsors; the polls are not independent surveys. Contemporaneous sources consistently list September 1, 2026 as the primary date, conflicting with September 15 in the supplied question. The August 18 voter guide was used only for its dated introductory schedule and open-seat context. No post-cutoff developments are included in the evidence pack.
